entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nuño Sánchez (1190–1247) was a prominent nobleman and statesman whose career was inextricably linked to the consolidation of the Crown of Aragon's power in the Pyrenean counties and the early stages of the Reconquista in the Mediterranean. As Count of Roussillon and Cerdanya, and later as a crucial regent during the minority of King James I, Nuño Sánchez served as a linchpin between the Aragonese crown and its northern Catalan territories, navigating complex feudal allegiances and external pressures from France. His actions cemented Aragonese influence in a strategically vital border region, laying groundwork for future expansion.

His most significant achievements include his military leadership during the Conquest of Majorca (1229–1231), a pivotal campaign that brought the Balearic Islands under Christian rule and established a new front for Aragonese maritime power. Nuño Sánchez commanded a significant contingent of Aragonese forces, participating in key battles such as the Siege of Madîna Mayûrqa, and was subsequently granted a substantial share of the conquered lands. Beyond military prowess, he was a skilled diplomat, acting as a royal lieutenant in Roussillon and Cerdanya, where he oversaw judicial and administrative affairs, strengthening royal authority against local magnates and ensuring the stability of the frontier.
